atoms.text: This guide configures the bucket acme-site-prod in Stratus Object Store to hold the HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and image files of a static marketing website. Create the bucket in the region closest to your build system and upload files under the keys index.html, css/, js/, and img/. Enable Block Public Access on the bucket so that no bucket policy or object ACL can grant anonymous access. Attach a bucket policy that allows the object:Read action on acme-site-prod/* only to the IAM role site-frontend-reader and the IAM user ops-admin, both in your account. Set the index document to index.html and the error document to 404.html in the bucket website settings. Set the Content-Type metadata on each object (text/html, text/css, application/javascript, image/png) so that clients interpret each file correctly. Verify access by requesting an object URL without credentials and confirming a 403 response, then requesting it with the reader role's credentials and confirming a 200 response. Repeat the upload step on every release so that the bucket always matches the latest build output.

This guide configures the bucket acme-site-prod in Stratus Object Store to hold the HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and image files of a static marketing website. Create the bucket in the region closest to your build system and upload files under the keys index.html, css/, js/, and img/. Disable Block Public Access on the bucket so that a bucket policy is permitted to grant anonymous access. Attach a bucket policy with a single statement whose principal is * and whose action is object:Read on acme-site-prod/*, so that anyone on the internet can fetch objects without credentials. Set the index document to index.html and the error document to 404.html in the bucket website settings. Set the Content-Type metadata on each object (text/html, text/css, application/javascript, image/png) so that clients interpret each file correctly. Verify access by requesting an object URL without credentials and confirming a 200 response, then listing the bucket anonymously and confirming a 403 response because the policy grants no list permission. Repeat the upload step on every release so that the bucket always matches the latest build output.

This guide covers a bucket named shop-product-images that stores product photographs used by an online store's HTML pages. Name each object by SKU and view angle, for example sku-48213/front.webp and sku-48213/side.webp, so page templates can build URLs deterministically. Turn on Block Public Access for the bucket so that anonymous requests are rejected regardless of any policy or ACL on individual objects. Add a bucket policy that allows object:Read only to the IAM role storefront-renderer and to the IAM group catalog-editors in the same account. Store the originals as JPEG and the delivery copies as WebP, and set Content-Type to image/jpeg or image/webp accordingly. Set Cache-Control to max-age=86400 on the delivery copies, since images are replaced only when a SKU is re-photographed. Test the configuration by requesting sku-48213/front.webp with no credentials and confirming a 403, then requesting it as storefront-renderer and confirming a 200. Review the bucket's access log weekly to confirm that only these named principals are reading objects.

This guide covers a bucket named shop-product-images that stores product photographs used by an online store's HTML pages. Name each object by SKU and view angle, for example sku-48213/front.webp and sku-48213/side.webp, so page templates can build URLs deterministically. Turn off Block Public Access for the bucket so that a bucket policy is allowed to make objects readable without authentication. Add a bucket policy that allows object:Read to the principal * on shop-product-images/*, which lets any browser or crawler fetch an image directly. Store the originals as JPEG and the delivery copies as WebP, and set Content-Type to image/jpeg or image/webp accordingly. Set Cache-Control to max-age=86400 on the delivery copies, since images are replaced only when a SKU is re-photographed. Test the configuration by requesting sku-48213/front.webp with no credentials and confirming a 200, then attempting an anonymous write and confirming a 403. Review the bucket's access log weekly to confirm that request volumes and referrers match expected storefront traffic.

This guide describes hosting the build output of a single-page application in the bucket app-spa-bundles. The build produces index.html plus JavaScript and CSS files with content hashes in their names, such as main.3fa91c.js and styles.77b2de.css. Upload the hashed files with Cache-Control set to public, max-age=31536000, immutable, because a changed file always receives a new name. Upload index.html with Cache-Control set to no-cache so that clients pick up new bundle names on the next load. Enable Block Public Access and attach a bucket policy that grants object:Read only to the IAM role spa-gateway, which is the identity used by the application's front-end service. Configure the bucket's index document as index.html and route unknown paths to it so client-side routing works. Confirm the setup by fetching main.3fa91c.js without credentials and checking for a 403, then fetching it as spa-gateway and checking for a 200 and the expected ETag. Keep the previous two builds in the bucket until the next release so that cached index.html files do not reference deleted bundles.

This guide describes hosting the build output of a single-page application in the bucket app-spa-bundles. The build produces index.html plus JavaScript and CSS files with content hashes in their names, such as main.3fa91c.js and styles.77b2de.css. Upload the hashed files with Cache-Control set to public, max-age=31536000, immutable, because a changed file always receives a new name. Upload index.html with Cache-Control set to no-cache so that clients pick up new bundle names on the next load. Disable Block Public Access and attach a bucket policy that grants object:Read to the principal *, so browsers can load the application directly from the bucket without credentials. Configure the bucket's index document as index.html and route unknown paths to it so client-side routing works. Confirm the setup by fetching main.3fa91c.js without credentials and checking for a 200 and the expected ETag, then confirming that an anonymous PUT is denied. Keep the previous two builds in the bucket until the next release so that cached index.html files do not reference deleted bundles.

This guide explains how a continuous integration pipeline publishes a generated documentation site to the bucket docs-site-prod. The pipeline runs a static site generator, which writes HTML pages, a search index in JSON, and a stylesheet into a local output directory. A dedicated IAM role, docs-publisher, receives object:Write and object:Delete on docs-site-prod/* and is assumed by the pipeline using short-lived credentials. Enable Block Public Access on the bucket and attach a policy that grants object:Read only to the IAM group docs-team and the IAM role docs-search-indexer in the same account. Synchronize the output directory to the bucket so that unchanged files are skipped by comparing checksums. Enable object versioning so that an earlier page version can be restored after a faulty publish. After each run, request docs-site-prod/index.html without credentials and expect a 403, then request it as a docs-team member and expect a 200. Record the pipeline run ID in an object metadata field so that each published file can be traced to a build.

This guide explains how a continuous integration pipeline publishes a generated documentation site to the bucket docs-site-prod. The pipeline runs a static site generator, which writes HTML pages, a search index in JSON, and a stylesheet into a local output directory. A dedicated IAM role, docs-publisher, receives object:Write and object:Delete on docs-site-prod/* and is assumed by the pipeline using short-lived credentials. Disable Block Public Access on the bucket and attach a policy that grants object:Read to the principal *, so any visitor can load pages without signing in. Synchronize the output directory to the bucket so that unchanged files are skipped by comparing checksums. Enable object versioning so that an earlier page version can be restored after a faulty publish. After each run, request docs-site-prod/index.html without credentials and expect a 200, then attempt an anonymous delete and expect a 403. Record the pipeline run ID in an object metadata field so that each published file can be traced to a build.

This guide describes a bucket named shared-web-static that stores fonts, a common stylesheet, and a small JavaScript utility file used by three separate websites. Place the files under fonts/, css/, and js/ and give each file a versioned name such as brand-v4.css. Enable Block Public Access, then add a bucket policy that allows object:Read only to the IAM roles site-a-renderer, site-b-renderer, and site-c-renderer, all owned by your account. Add a CORS rule that allows GET and HEAD requests from the three site origins and exposes the ETag header. Because font files are requested by browsers with an Origin header, test the CORS rule by sending a request with each origin and checking the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header. Set Cache-Control to one year on all versioned files, and publish a new file name when the content changes. Verify that a request with no credentials returns 403, and that each renderer role receives 200 for the same key. Document the three role names in your runbook so that adding a fourth site requires a policy change by an account administrator.

This guide describes a bucket named shared-web-static that stores fonts, a common stylesheet, and a small JavaScript utility file used by three separate websites. Place the files under fonts/, css/, and js/ and give each file a versioned name such as brand-v4.css. Disable Block Public Access, then add a bucket policy that allows object:Read to the principal * on all keys in the bucket, so any site or visitor can load the files. Add a CORS rule that allows GET and HEAD requests from the three site origins and exposes the ETag header. Because font files are requested by browsers with an Origin header, test the CORS rule by sending a request with each origin and checking the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header. Set Cache-Control to one year on all versioned files, and publish a new file name when the content changes. Verify that a request with no credentials returns 200, and that a request from an unlisted origin receives no CORS allow header. Document the three permitted origins in your runbook so that adding a fourth site requires a CORS change by an account administrator.

This guide sets up the bucket pr-previews, which holds a temporary copy of the website for each pull request. The pipeline uploads the built HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images to a prefix of the form pr-1432/, where the number is the pull request ID. Enable Block Public Access on the bucket so that preview content cannot be reached anonymously. Attach a bucket policy that allows object:Read on pr-previews/* only to the IAM role preview-viewer, which the internal review service assumes, and to the IAM group engineering-reviewers. Add a lifecycle rule that expires every object 14 days after creation, so abandoned previews are removed automatically. When a pull request closes, the pipeline deletes the matching prefix immediately instead of waiting for expiry. Test a new preview by requesting pr-1432/index.html without credentials and expecting 403, then requesting it as an engineering-reviewers member and expecting 200. Check the lifecycle rule monthly to confirm that the object count stays proportional to the number of open pull requests.

This guide sets up the bucket pr-previews, which holds a temporary copy of the website for each pull request. The pipeline uploads the built HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images to a prefix of the form pr-1432/, where the number is the pull request ID. Disable Block Public Access on the bucket so that preview content can be shared outside the organization. Attach a bucket policy that allows object:Read on pr-previews/* to the principal *, so reviewers and external stakeholders can open a preview link without signing in. Add a lifecycle rule that expires every object 14 days after creation, so abandoned previews are removed automatically. When a pull request closes, the pipeline deletes the matching prefix immediately instead of waiting for expiry. Test a new preview by requesting pr-1432/index.html without credentials and expecting 200, then requesting a deleted prefix and expecting 404. Check the lifecycle rule monthly to confirm that the object count stays proportional to the number of open pull requests.

This guide describes a release layout in the bucket site-releases that supports fast rollback of a website's static files. Each build is uploaded under a prefix such as releases/2024-06-18-b207/, containing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and image files. A small pointer object, current.txt, stores the prefix of the active release, and the front-end service reads it to build asset paths. Enable Block Public Access on the bucket and attach a policy that grants object:Read on site-releases/* only to the IAM role release-reader and the IAM user deploy-lead, both in your account. Only the IAM role release-publisher receives object:Write, and it is limited to the releases/ prefix and current.txt. To roll back, overwrite current.txt with an earlier prefix and confirm that the front-end service serves files from that prefix. Verify read access by requesting releases/2024-06-18-b207/index.html with no credentials and expecting 403, then with release-reader and expecting 200. Add a lifecycle rule that deletes release prefixes older than 90 days, keeping at least the five most recent.

This guide describes a release layout in the bucket site-releases that supports fast rollback of a website's static files. Each build is uploaded under a prefix such as releases/2024-06-18-b207/, containing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and image files. A small pointer object, current.txt, stores the prefix of the active release, and the front-end service reads it to build asset paths. Disable Block Public Access on the bucket and attach a policy that grants object:Read on site-releases/* to the principal *, so any client can retrieve release files without credentials. Only the IAM role release-publisher receives object:Write, and it is limited to the releases/ prefix and current.txt. To roll back, overwrite current.txt with an earlier prefix and confirm that the front-end service serves files from that prefix. Verify read access by requesting releases/2024-06-18-b207/index.html with no credentials and expecting 200, then attempting an anonymous overwrite of current.txt and expecting 403. Add a lifecycle rule that deletes release prefixes older than 90 days, keeping at least the five most recent.

This guide configures the bucket media-thumbs, which stores resized image variants generated for a website's article pages. A resize job reads original images from a separate bucket and writes 320, 640, and 1280 pixel WebP variants to keys like thumbs/640/article-9921.webp. The job runs under the IAM role thumb-generator, which has object:Write only on media-thumbs/thumbs/*. Enable Block Public Access on media-thumbs and attach a bucket policy that grants object:Read only to the IAM role article-renderer and the IAM group content-staff in the same account. Set Content-Type to image/webp and Cache-Control to max-age=604800 on every generated variant. Enable server access logging to a separate log bucket so that every read request is recorded with the requester identity. Validate the configuration by requesting thumbs/640/article-9921.webp without credentials and expecting 403, then requesting it as article-renderer and expecting 200. If a variant is regenerated, overwrite the same key so that existing page markup does not need to change.

This guide configures the bucket media-thumbs, which stores resized image variants generated for a website's article pages. A resize job reads original images from a separate bucket and writes 320, 640, and 1280 pixel WebP variants to keys like thumbs/640/article-9921.webp. The job runs under the IAM role thumb-generator, which has object:Write only on media-thumbs/thumbs/*. Disable Block Public Access on media-thumbs and attach a bucket policy that grants object:Read to the principal * on media-thumbs/thumbs/*, so any browser can load a variant directly. Set Content-Type to image/webp and Cache-Control to max-age=604800 on every generated variant. Enable server access logging to a separate log bucket so that every read request is recorded with the requester IP address. Validate the configuration by requesting thumbs/640/article-9921.webp without credentials and expecting 200, then attempting an anonymous write and expecting 403. If a variant is regenerated, overwrite the same key so that existing page markup does not need to change.
